items.label: text
items.text: Aluminium is above carbon in the reactivity series and so heating aluminium oxide with carbon will not produce a reaction. Aluminium must be extracted by electrolysis. Al³+ + 3e- → Al

items.label: list_item
items.text: Sodium is high in the reactivity series, and so will need to be produced by electrolysis. It can be manufactured by electrolysing molten sodium chloride using suitable electrodes (industrially, carbon anode, steel cathode), keeping the sodium and chlorine apart to prevent them from reacting back to give sodium chloride again.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Sodium would be released at the cathode: Na+(l) + e− → Na(l)

items.label: list_item
items.text: b It needed the discovery of electricity.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Any other metals high in the reactivity series – e.g. potassium, lithium, calcium, magnesium.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Because lead is below iron in the reactivity series it is also below carbon. Lead can be extracted from its ore by heating with carbon.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Chromium(Ill) oxide contains the Cr^3+ ion. The oxide ion has the formula O²-, therefore the formula of chromium(III) oxide is Cr2O3. Cr2}O3+ 2Al → 2Cr + Al2O3}

items.label: list_item
items.text: Al is the reducing agent because it takes the O away from the Cr2O3 - it reduces it.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Chromium is less reactive than aluminium because the aluminium is able to take the oxygen away from the chromium oxide.

items.text: b TiCl4}+ 2Mg → MgCl2} + Ti

items.label: list_item
items.text: Magnesium is more reactive than titanium as it is able to take the chlorine away from the TiCl4; the magnesium is able to reduce the TiCl4.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Magnesium is more reactive than carbon, so it could be extracted from its ore by electrolysis or by heating with a more reactive metal such as sodium.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Titanium is more expensive than magnesium. Although it is expensive to extract magnesium using electrolysis, the magnesium is used in the extraction of titanium, therefore titanium must be more expensive.

items.label: list_item
items.text: It has a low density. (Note: saying that it has a low density is usually better than just saying it is light)

items.label: list_item
items.text: li Alloys are stronger than the pure metals. Alloys contain some atoms of different sizes; this makes it more difficult for the layers of positive ions to slide over each other.

items.label: list_item
items.text: iii Advantages:

items.label: list_item
items.text: An aluminium body is lighter than a steel body and so the car will use less fuel. An aluminium body will not corrode.

items.label: text
items.text: Disadvantage:

items.label: list_item
items.text: Aluminium is more expensive than steel.

items.label: list_item
items.text: a good conductor of electricity and ductile (can be drawn out into wires)

items.label: list_item
items.text: ii does not react with water and malleable (can be hammered into shape)

items.label: list_item
items.text: High-carbon steel is brittle and not very malleable so it would be difficult to make it into the correct shapes for car bodies. It would also not bend/deform very well during a crash - the fact that mild steel deforms upon impact (because it is malleable) is important for absorbing some of the force upon impact (from a Physics point of view, the change in momentum occurs over a longer period of time).
